name: Split view
first: A view that shows a list and the details of the chosen item side by side when there is room, and collapses into one stack of screens when there is not.

dependsOn.why: On a narrow screen, a split view collapses its columns into one navigation stack.
dependsOn.whyInExample: On an iPhone, the sidebar of `split` would be the root view of a stack, as `list` is on the page of Navigation stack.

what.is: A `NavigationSplitView` is a view that shows two or three columns side by side: a sidebar, which usually lists items, and a detail column, which shows the item the user chose. Apple's documentation says that at narrow sizes, such as on an iPhone, it collapses its columns into one stack of screens.
what.afterExample: This program runs on a Mac, where there is room for both columns, so the split view shows the sidebar and the detail side by side.
what.problem: On an iPad or a Mac, a list and the details of one item fit side by side, and the user picks items without leaving the list. On an iPhone they do not fit. A split view is written once, and shows columns where there is room and a stack of screens where there is not.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that people choose an item in a leading column to show its details in the following columns. At narrow sizes, the split view collapses all its columns into a stack, and shows the last column that has something useful to show.

when.text: Use it for the main screen of an app that lists items and shows one in detail, when the app runs on an iPad or a Mac as well as an iPhone.
Don't use it for an app that only runs on an iPhone. There it is always one stack, and a navigation stack is simpler.

parts.name: The sidebar, lines 3 to 6
parts.text: The first braces after `NavigationSplitView` hold the sidebar, the leading column. Here it is a `Text`, Trips. In an app it is usually a list of the items the user chooses from.

parts.name: The detail, lines 6 to 9
parts.text: The braces after the argument label `detail:` hold the detail column, the trailing column, which shows the chosen item. Here it is a `Text`, Lima.

steps.text: Line 3 makes a split view with two columns: the sidebar, in its first braces, and the detail, after `detail:`.
Line 10 makes a renderer and draws the split view. There is room for both columns, so it shows both. The sidebar appears, and line 5 prints {{shows the sidebar}}.
The detail appears beside it, and line 8 prints {{shows the detail}}.

end.text: With room for both, the split view showed the sidebar and the detail side by side.
